item.description: Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was struck by drones launched from Iraq, with the latest squeeze reverberating through the region Saturday as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels threatened to deepen the world’s energy crisis.

media:content.media:text: Image: A 60-mile smoke plume along the route of the East-West oil pipeline, south of Medina
media:content.media:description: A 60-mile smoke plume along the route of the East-West oil pipeline, south of Medina

media:content.media:text: Round metallic storage tanks and pipelines in a desert landscape.
media:content.media:description: A crude oil processing facility in Abqaiq, one terminus of the East-West pipeline in Saudi Arabia. The 745-mile pipeline, which the country shut down on Friday, had helped to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

media:content.media:text: TOPSHOT-YEMEN-CONFLICT
media:content.media:description: A Houthi recruitment march in Sanaa, Yemen, on Thursday. If the Houthis are able to threaten shipping along the Bab el Mandeb Strait, it could reduce oil supplies through another key waterway.

media:content.media:text: APTOPIX Iran War Strait of Hormuz
media:content.media:description: Iran on Saturday said that it would sign an agreement with Oman over a joint route through the Strait of Hormuz Monday, part of a deal that would secure future navigation rights.

media:content.media:text: A makeshift shelter of grass and sticks and blankets in the desert.
media:content.media:description: The United Nations’ International Organization for Migration warned Friday at least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week.

item.title: Saudi shutdown of key pipeline limits oil flow as Yemen hits back against Houthis
